item.subject: maths
item.stem:
Lila looks at the diagram. Line $m$ is given, point $P$ is off $m$, and transversal $t$ cuts $m$ at $E$. The marked angle $\alpha$ at $E$ is copied at $P$ so that new line $n$ through $P$ makes the corresponding angle $\alpha$ with $t$.

Which claim correctly states what that construction produces?

options.A: Copy an angle at $P$ with no transversal that cuts line $m$, and claim the new line is parallel to $m$.
options.B: Say that the finished parallel line is what creates transversal $t$ through $m$.
options.C: Line $n$ through $P$ is parallel to $m$, because the corresponding angle $\alpha$ was copied from transversal $t$.
options.D: Slide a set-square along $m$ and treat that tool method as this corresponding-angle copy.
